title: Deep winter: clear, dry and cold
text: Days are bright but short, and nights above 3,000 m sit well below freezing. High passes such as the Thorong La, Cho La and Larkya La are often blocked by snow. Lower ridge treks and the Kathmandu Valley rim are at their clearest.

title: Late winter: still cold, slowly opening
text: Mostly clear, with snow lingering on shaded trails and the high passes. Lodges on quieter routes begin to reopen towards the end of the month, and rhododendrons start to flower below 2,500 m.

title: Spring begins
text: Temperatures climb and the main trails get busy again. Rhododendron forest blooms through the mid-hills. Expect some afternoon cloud and haze, and old snow on passes above 5,000 m early in the month.

title: Peak spring season
text: Warm days, long light and settled mornings, with cloud building most afternoons. Everest Base Camp fills with expeditions. The low valleys are hot and hazy, so start early.

title: Late spring: warm and hazy
text: The warmest month at altitude and a good one for high passes, but haze, afternoon thunderstorms and pre-monsoon showers increase as the weeks go on. Low approaches are hot.

title: The monsoon arrives
text: Rain usually sets in during the second week. Cloud, leeches and landslides affect most trails south of the main range, and flights are often delayed. The rain-shadow regions of Mustang and Dolpo come into season.

title: Full monsoon
text: Heavy rain most days, frequent road and flight disruption, and few mountain views. Upper Mustang, Nar Phu and Dolpo stay comparatively dry and are the sensible choices.

title: Monsoon continues
text: Warm, wet and very green, with swollen rivers and quiet trails. Stick to the rain-shadow regions, or keep your dates flexible and expect to wait out bad days.

title: The rain withdraws
text: Early September is still wet and cloudy. By the end of the month the air clears and the autumn season opens. Trails and bridges can be damaged from the summer, so ask about recent conditions.

title: Peak autumn season
text: The clearest skies and most settled weather of the year. Trails, flights and lodges are at their busiest, so book ahead. A late storm can still drop sudden heavy snow at altitude.

title: Late autumn: dry, clear and cooler
text: Stable weather continues with fewer people after the middle of the month. Nights above 4,000 m are cold, and high passes can close after the first big snowfall.

title: Early winter
text: Crisp, clear days and quiet trails. It is cold above 3,000 m, some high lodges close for the season and the passes become unreliable. A good month for lower and mid-altitude routes.
